The '''2013 Tippeligaen''' was the 69th completed season of top division [[association football|football]] in Norway. The competition began 15 March 2013 and ended on 10 November 2013, when [[Strømsgodset Toppfotball|Strømsgodset]] defeated [[FK Haugesund|Haugesund]] 4–0 to win their second league title.

The league was contested by 16 teams: The best 13 teams of the [[2012 Tippeligaen|2012 season]], [[IK Start|Start]] and [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg 08]] who won promotion from the [[2012 1. divisjon]] and [[Sandnes Ulf]] who retained their spot in the top league after beating the [[1. divisjon]] side [[Ullensaker/Kisa IL|Ullensaker/Kisa]] in the relegation play-off.

[[Molde FK|Molde]] who won Tippeligaen the previous season failed to defend the championship and ended on sixth place. [[Strømsgodset Toppfotball|Strømsgodset]] who won silver in 2012, won their first league championship in 43 years, finishing one point ahead of title contenders [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]]. [[FK Haugesund|Haugesund]] won bronze for the first time in the history, while [[Tromsø IL|Tromsø]] and [[Hønefoss BK|Hønefoss]] were relegated to the [[2014 1. divisjon]].

==Background==
{{See also|2012 Tippeligaen}}
[[Molde FK|Molde]], [[Strømsgodset Toppfotball|Strømsgodset]] and [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] were involved in the title race in the [[2012 Tippeligaen|2012 season]]. After Rosenborg lost against the other title contenders Molde and Strømsgodset in the 27th and the 28th round respectively,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.tv2.no/sport/fotball/tippeligaen/solskjaer-med-mesterligafeiring-da-molde-koblet-gullgrepet-3910980.html |language=no |title=Solskjær med Mesterliga-feiring da Molde koblet gullgrepet |newspaper=TV 2 |first1=Morten |last1=Stokstad |first2=Mats |last2=Wederwang |date=28 October 2012 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/norsk/artikkel.php?artid=10047667 |language=no |title=Her sendes Rosenborg ut av gullkampen |newspaper=Verdens Gang |first=Mikal |last=Aaserud |date=4 November 2012 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> Molde secured their second straight Tippeligaen title with one match left to play when Strømsgodset lost against [[Sandnes Ulf]]. [[Fredrikstad FK|Fredrikstad]] and [[Stabæk Fotball|Stabæk]] were relegated after finishing 15th and 16th respectively, while [[Sandnes Ulf]] had to play a relegation play-off against the [[1. divisjon]] side [[Ullensaker/Kisa IL|Ullensaker/Kisa]],<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nrk.no/sport/fotball/fredrikstad-rykket-ned-1.8401004 |language=no |title=Fredrikstad rykket ned fra eliteserien: – Vi er veldig lei oss |newspaper=NRK |first=Steinar Andre |last=Danielsen |date=18 November 2012 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> which they won 7–1 on aggregate.

After the 2012 season, Rosenborg's head coach [[Jan Jönsson]] was fired from his position, and was replaced by the head coach of the successful [[Norway national under-21 football team|Norwegian under-21 team]], [[Per Joar Hansen]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nettavisen.no/sport/fotball/article3531969.ece |language=no |title=Nå er han Rosenborg-trener |newspaper=Nettavisen |date=14 December 2012 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> Jönsson was soon appointed as head coach of [[Aalesunds FK|Aalesund]], as a replacement for [[Kjetil Rekdal]] who had also been fired. Rekdal returned to his old club [[Vålerenga Fotball|Vålerenga]], which he won the league with in [[2005 Tippeligaen|2005]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nrk.no/sport/fotball/rekdal-ny-trener-for-valerenga-1.10865100|language=no |title=Rekdal tilbake i Vålerenga: – Motivasjonen min er enorm |newspaper=NRK |first=Bjørnar |last=Hjellen |date=8 January 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> [[Martin Andresen]] had announced in October 2012 that he would leave his position as manager of Vålerenga after the season.,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/norsk/artikkel.php?artid=10062327 |language=no |title=Andresen ferdig i Vålerenga |newspaper=Verdens Gang |first=Marius |last=Vik |date=15 October 2012 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> In addition [[Per-Mathias Høgmo]] left [[Tromsø IL|Tromsø]] after his contract expired, and they appointed [[Agnar Christensen]] as the new head coach.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dagbladet.no/2012/09/28/sport/fotball/tippeligaen/agnar_christensen/per-mathias_hogmo/23624024/ |language=no |title=Høgmo-assistent er TILs nye trener |newspaper=Dagbladet |first=Gorm S. |last=Andersen |date=28 September 2012 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref>

==Season summary==
Ahead of each Tippeligaen season, the newspapers in Norway predict how the season is going to end. In 2013, all of the major newspapers predicted that either Molde or Rosenborg would win the league.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.bt.no/100Sport/fotball/eliteserien/Scheie-med-mest-peiling_-TV-2-og-Dagbladet-pa-bunn-402643_1.snd |language=no |title=Scheie med mest peiling, TV 2 og Dagbladet på bunn |newspaper=Bergens Tidende |first=Roar |last=Lyngøy |date=12 November 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> The opening match of the 2013 season was played between [[Viking FK|Viking]] and the defending champions Molde in [[Stavanger]]. Viking won the match 2–1 after a match-winning goal by [[Trond Olsen]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dagbladet.no/2013/03/15/sport/fotball/tippeligaen/molde/viking/26234754/ |language=no |title=– En bonus å slå den regjerende mesteren |newspaper=Dagbladet |first=Fredrik Økstad |last=Sandberg |date=15 March 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> Molde became the first defending champion in Norway to lose the first four matches of the season, with their manager [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]] stating that the club wouldn't be able to defend the title.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nettavisen.no/sport/fotball/article3607326.ece |language=no |title=– Klubben, fansen og regionen kan bare glemme det |newspaper=Nettavisen |first=Øyvind Garnes |last=Loftheim |date=13 April 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> After collecting two points in the first seven matches,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.smp.no/100Sport/fotball/eliteserien/--Var-beste-mulighet-pa-mange-ar-321868_1.snd |language=no |title=– Vår beste mulighet på mange år |newspaper=Sunnmørsposten |first=Kristian |last=Stenerud |date=8 May 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131112165512/http://www.smp.no/100Sport/fotball/eliteserien/--Var-beste-mulighet-pa-mange-ar-321868_1.snd |archive-date=12 November 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Molde won their first match 4–1 against local rivals [[Aalesunds FK|Aalesund]]. Aalesund had an impressing season opener, by winning four of the first four matches, and after the loss against Molde they won 7–1 against [[Lillestrøm SK|Lillestrøm]] with [[Abderrazak Hamdallah]] scoring a hat-trick, and was positioned second after nine matches.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.aftenposten.no/100Sport/fotball/eliteserien/Aalesund-vant-7-1-over-Lillestrom-322138_1.snd |language=no |title=Aalesund vant 7–1 over Lillestrøm |newspaper=Aftenposten |first=Pål Are |last=Lilleheim |date=13 May 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref>

With Molde out of the race for the title, it looked as though it was going to be a fight between Strømsgodset and Rosenborg.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aftenposten.no/100Sport/fotball/eliteserien/Her-er-ti-ting-vi-husker-fra-arets-sesong-402498_1.snd |title=Her er ti ting vi husker fra årets sesong – Aftenposten |website=aftenposten.no |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131112114111/http://www.aftenposten.no/100Sport/fotball/eliteserien/Her-er-ti-ting-vi-husker-fra-arets-sesong-402498_1.snd |archive-date=2013-11-12}}</ref> Aalesund were, however, only five points behind the leaders Rosenborg, after they won three consecutive matches away from home, and with 10 matches left to play the players started to talk about winning the league.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.smp.no/100Sport/fotball/eliteserien/Na-tor-Aalesund-a-snakke-om-gull-388101_1.snd |title = Nå tør Aalesund å snakke om gull -smp.no – nyheter, sport, kultur og økonomi  |access-date=13 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131113103211/http://www.smp.no/100Sport/fotball/eliteserien/Na-tor-Aalesund-a-snakke-om-gull-388101_1.snd |archive-date=13 November 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> After Aalesund lost three matches in a row, the team was too far behind the top two teams, and three points behind Viking in third place.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dagbladet.no/2013/09/28/sport/fotball/aalesund/brann/29511197/|title = – Det blir tøft å ta medalje nå|date = 28 September 2013}}</ref> Aalesund went seven matches without winning, but with a record-high number of points the club finished the season in fourth place.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aftenposten.no/100Sport/fotball/eliteserien/Jnssson-fornoyd-med-poengrekord-402422_1.snd |title=Jönssson fornøyd med poengrekord – Aftenposten |website=aftenposten.no |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131113105013/http://www.aftenposten.no/100Sport/fotball/eliteserien/Jnssson-fornoyd-med-poengrekord-402422_1.snd |archive-date=2013-11-13}}</ref>

Tromsø, who finished fourth and lost the [[2012 Norwegian Football Cup Final|Norwegian Cup Final]] in the previous season, were the only Norwegian team to qualify for the [[2013–14 UEFA Europa League]] group stage, but their form in the league after the summer break was declining, and they soon found themselves fighting against relegation. The team did however manage to put an end to Rosenborg's streak of 16 matches without losing, when Tromsø won 1–0 at home.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nrk.no/sport/fotball/rosenborg-smell-mot-tromso-1.11243208|title=Rosenborg-smell mot Tromsø|date=15 September 2013}}</ref> After the loss at home against [[IK Start|Start]] in the 25th round, Tromsø had collected six points in the last 12 matches and the club fired the head coach Agnar Christensen and replaced him with [[Steinar Nilsen]], who had saved the team from relegation in 2005 and 2006.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nettavisen.no/sport/fotball/article3687762.ece |language=no |title=Disse tar over Tromsø |newspaper=Nettavisen |agency=Norwegian News Agency |date=1 October 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103214835/http://www.nettavisen.no/sport/fotball/article3687762.ece |archive-date=3 November 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

For the first time since the 2005 season, the championship was determined in the decisive match of the season.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.bt.no/100Sport/fotball/eliteserien/Her-er-de-10-mest-dramatiske-seriefinaler-402009_1.snd |language=no |title=Drama til siste minutt |newspaper=Bergens Tidende |first=Roy |last=Ellingsen |date=9 November 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> Strømsgodset were leading the league one point ahead of Rosenborg, and could secure the championship in the home-match against bronze-winners [[FK Haugesund|Haugesund]]. At the same time, six teams were not safe from relegation with one match left to play; the three teams Sarpsborg 08, Tromsø and Hønefoss were fighting to avoid the two direct relegation spots, while Vålerenga, Sogndal and Sandnes Ulf could still be forced to play a relegation play-off against a 1. divisjon side if they finished 14th in the league.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nrk.no/sport/fotball/seks-lag-kan-rykke-ned-1.11335653 |language=no |title=Innrømmer at VIF-jobben er tyngre enn han trodde |newspaper=NRK |first1=Anders Rove |last1=Berntsen |first2=Aslak Rune |last2=Eikrem |date=4 November 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> Rosenborg was leading 2–0 at half-time against Lillestrøm, and Strømsgodset needed to score a goal in their match against Haugesund to secure the title. [[Ola Kamara]] sent Strømsgodset up in a 1–0 lead, and after [[Stefan Johansen]] and [[Øyvind Storflor]] scored one goal each and [[Ola Kamara]] scored his second goal in the game, Strømsgodset won the match 4–0 and secured their first championship since the [[1970 Norwegian First Division|1970 season]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.aftenposten.no/100Sport/fotball/eliteserien/Gull-til-Godset-402352_1.snd |language=no |title=Gull til Godset |newspaper=Aftenposten |first=Ole Kåre |last=Eide |date=10 November 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> Tromsø had to win the match away against [[SK Brann|Brann]], who had nothing to play for in the last round, to avoid relegation but Tromsø had not won a single match away from home during the season, and also lost the last match 4–1, and were relegated to the 1. divisjon after an 11-year-long spell in the top flight. Hønefoss also had to win their last match to avoid relegation, and were leading the match against Odd, but [[Frode Johnsen]] scored the match-winning goal and Odd won 3–2. Sarpborg 08 lost the last match 2–1 against Viking, despite leading when the [[stoppage time]] began, and finished 14th in the league, and a met the 1. divisjon side [[Ranheim Fotball|Ranheim]] in the [[#Relegation play-offs|relegation play-off]] They won 1–0 at home and 2–0 in the awaygame and play in the next seasons Tippeligaen.<ref name="relegation">{{cite news |url=http://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/norsk/artikkel.php?artid=10153360 |language=no |title=TILs landslagsback: – Blytungt og uvirkelig |newspaper=Verdens Gang |first1=Øystein |last1=Hernes |first2=Henrik |last2=Horjen |first3=Erik Haugen |last3=Aspaas |first4=Joar |last4=Time |date=10 November 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref>

Johnsen's goal against Hønefoss was his sixteenth overall this season, and he became top goalscorer with one more goal than Aalesund's Hamdallah. Aged 38, Johnsen is the oldest-ever top goalscorer in the Norwegian top flight.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/artikkel.php?artid=10153379 |language=no |title=Europas eldste toppscorer noensinne |newspaper=Verdens Gang |first=Erik Haugen |last=Aspaas |date=10 November 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref> Johnsen also won the [[Kniksen Award]] for the "forward of the year". Players from Strømsgodset won four of the five Kniksen Award prices as [[Adam Larsen Kwarasey]] won the goalkeeper of the year, [[Lars Christopher Vilsvik]] was named defender of the year, [[Stefan Johansen]] was the midfielder of the year and the head coach, [[Ronny Deila]], won the "manager of the year" award.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nettavisen.no/sport/fotball/article3709569.ece |language=no |title=Strømsgodset i et ekslusivt selskap |newspaper=Nettavisen |first=Christina Paulos |last=Syversen |date=10 November 2013 |access-date=12 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131113214335/http://www.nettavisen.no/sport/fotball/article3709569.ece |archive-date=13 November 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Teams==
Sixteen teams competed in the league – the top fourteen teams from the previous season and the two teams promoted from the [[2012 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]] The promoted teams were [[IK Start|Start]] and [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg 08]] (both returning after a season's absence). They replaced [[Fredrikstad FK|Fredrikstad]] (ending their two-year spell in the top flight) and [[Stabæk Fotball|Stabæk]] (relegated after seven years in the top flight).

==Relegation play-offs==
{{main|2013 Eliteserien promotion/relegation play-offs}}
The 14th-placed team, [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg 08]], took part in a two-legged play-off against [[Ranheim Fotball|Ranheim]], the winners of the 2013 1. divisjon [[2013 Norwegian First Division#Promotion play-offs|promotion play-offs]], to decide who would play in the [[2014 Tippeligaen]].

;First leg
